EnvelopeRequest.description:
A new version of the envelope.

There is no `version` field, and that is the point: which version this is
is a fact about the record, not a claim the caller gets to make. A body
that carried one would let two clients both write version 4 and one of them
silently lose.
EnvelopeRequest.title: EnvelopeRequest

EnvelopeRequirement.description: One class of action a human must approve before Master may take it.
EnvelopeRequirement.title: EnvelopeRequirement

Evidence.description:
One claim, its class, and what supports it.

`claim_class` keeps observation and speculation apart. A `FACT` must cite a
source that was read; an `INFERENCE` must say what it was inferred from; a
`HYPOTHESIS` is allowed to rest on nothing yet, which is exactly what makes
it a hypothesis rather than a finding.
Evidence.title: Evidence

EvidenceSource.description:
One place a claim came from, as it was actually reached.

The fields that matter most are the ones that are easy to fake:
`retrieved_at` (when it was read, not when it was written down),
`content_hash` (the bytes that were read), and `access_status` (whether it
was read at all).
EvidenceSource.title: EvidenceSource

EvidenceSourceTier.description: Source quality tiers, A (strongest) to D (weakest).
EvidenceSourceTier.title: EvidenceSourceTier

EvidenceView.description: One claim together with every source it cites.
EvidenceView.title: EvidenceView

ExecutionAttempt.description:
One try at the work.

Retries are recorded as separate attempts rather than as a counter, because
the interesting question after a failure is usually what differed between
the attempts.
ExecutionAttempt.title: ExecutionAttempt

ExecutionRecord.description:
The immutable record of one execution.

Written once, when the work ends — by delivery, by failure, by cancellation,
or by an open deviation. It references the contract version it ran under,
so a later change to what workers may do cannot rewrite what this one did.
ExecutionRecord.title: ExecutionRecord

client_message_id.description: Chosen once by the client; a retry with the same value is the same draft.
client_message_id.title: Client Message Id

MailDraft.title: MailDraft

MailView.description: One mail Action, its content, and whether a human must reconcile it.
MailView.title: MailView

MasterMessage.description:
One thing said between a person and Master, in the order it was said.

The conversation is recorded here rather than read back out of the harness,
for the reason a checkpoint is: a DSH session dies with its process and
cannot be resumed across one, so a conversation kept only there would
vanish at the moment somebody wants to read what was decided. `docs/04`
also makes the point the other way round — DSH session is not Project — and
a transcript stored in the harness would be exactly that confusion.

A row is one utterance, and it is append-only like everything else. Nothing
edits a message and nothing unsays one, which is what lets a later reader
treat the transcript as a record of what was actually said rather than of
what somebody last thought should have been said.

`turn_id` groups a question with whatever answering it produced. Master may
take several turns' worth of tool calls before it says anything, so the
reply is not necessarily one message, and a grouping that was inferred from
timestamps would be a guess.
MasterMessage.title: MasterMessage

NewProject.description:
What a person must say to open a project.

Both fields are required and neither has a default. The objective is what
Master plans against, so a project without one is a project whose first
turn has nothing to plan from, and `"Untitled"` would be a title RAVEL
invented rather than one somebody chose.
NewProject.title: NewProject

NodeView.description:
One node of the DAG, as a reader sees it.

A subset of `DagNode` rather than the whole record, and that is the one
place this module narrows. A node carries its contract references, its
join policy and its failure policy — all of which are how the node is
*executed* — and a DAG view is for reading what the project is doing, not
for re-deriving how it would be run. What is kept is what a person needs in
order to follow the graph: what the node is for, who executes it, what it
depends on, and where it has got to.
NodeView.title: NodeView

PauseRequest.description: Why the project is being stopped. Recorded, and may be empty.
PauseRequest.title: PauseRequest

ProjectSummary.description: One project, as it appears in a list.
ProjectSummary.title: ProjectSummary

RefreshRequest.description: The grant handed back by a previous login or refresh.
RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest

TokenPair.description:
What a successful authentication returns.

Both halves are returned because they answer different needs: the access
token is what a client sends on every request and cannot be revoked, and
the refresh token is single-use and is what a client keeps. A client handed
only the first would have to log in again within the hour; one handed only
the second would refresh before every request.
TokenPair.title: TokenPair

TurnView.description: One exchange, and whether this response replayed a stored one.
TurnView.title: TurnView

UserRole.description: The three V0 user roles. No complex RBAC.
UserRole.title: UserRole

Every project the caller is a member of, ordered by identifier.

The ordering is by identifier rather than by the membership's grant time
because the cursor has to name a key that cannot move: a grant time is
stable too, but it is not in the legacy projection, and adding a field to
that projection to make this page deterministic would change the shape the
TUI reads. Project identifiers are opaque and unique, which is enough for a
stable keyset.

Record the question, run one Master turn, record the answer if there is one.

The question is committed before the turn starts, so a turn that dies leaves
an unanswered question rather than no question. The advisory lock covers the
check-and-insert only; it is not held across the model turn, because holding
a transaction open for minutes would block every writer to the project for a
reason that has nothing to do with them.

get.description:
The whole project view, with `anchor_seq` read from the same transaction.

`anchor_seq` is the last event sequence the aggregate reflects. A client
stores it and reconnects the event stream with `after_seq=anchor_seq`, so
every event that arrived after the snapshot is delivered exactly once and
no event already reflected in the snapshot is replayed into it.

The source record, and bytes ``[offset, offset+limit)`` of its snapshot.

`next_offset` is present only when more bytes remain; a caller pages through
the content with it. The bytes are decoded as UTF-8 with replacement so a
text source reads as text; a binary source is still returned this way and
the `media_type` in the record tells the reader what it was.
